dev_ilir_pexmatched_singleL family — PEX baseline + two generic-pad retunes

One circuit (the validated, fed-back common-gate dev_ilir_pexmatched_singleL design), three branches differing only in pad model and how much of the matching network gets re-tuned for it.

cgdegLloadL_cscascloadL_noBuf_pex now carries this circuit unchanged, verified to reproduce dev_ilir_pexmatched_singleL's own historical report (S11/S21/S22/NF within 0.5 dB) against the real 0Ω PEX pad. gen_v1 and gen_v2 branch from it, swap to the generic pad, and re-tune increasingly more of the matching network to recover the match that pad swap costs.

Topology

cgdegLloadL_cscascloadL_noBuf_pex — 0Ω PEX pad, as-validated matching (unchanged from dev_ilir_pexmatched_singleL)
gen_v1 — generic pad, re-tuned: LEQ/RLEQ, LSHUNT_OUT/RLSHOUT, C15, C11
gen_v2 — generic pad, gen_v1's set + L1/Rs and LD2/RLD2

Retune methodology

Same cost function as elsewhere this session: penalize S11/S22 worse than −10 dB, reward S21, lightly penalize NF, evaluated on a 21-point 2.3–2.5 GHz sweep per candidate (full broadband/stability reserved for the final point). Every tunable inductor's series resistance is derived as R = ωL⁄Q with Q=12 at 2.4 GHz — except RLD2 in gen_v2, which had to be freed from that convention (see below).

gen_v1 — pad-facing network only (4 free parameters)

LEQ, LSHUNT_OUT, C15, C11. L1/Rs and the two drain-peaking tanks (LD4/RLD3, LD2/RLD2) carried over unchanged from the PEX-matched branch. ~10,500 evaluations (broad search + two local-refinement rounds) converged on LEQ=1.57 nH, LSHUNT_OUT=4.06 nH, C15=1.56 pF, C11=3.08 pF.

Tested and rejected your hypothesis that removing the input/output shunt inductors would help against the generic pad's lower parasitic loading: setting them near-zero shorts the node to ground (S21 collapses to −60 dB); setting them very large (near-open) also underperforms (S11 only −0.9 dB). Every search, from every starting point, converges back to properly-sized, properly-tuned shunt stubs — they're load-bearing, not PEX-specific baggage.

gen_v2 — + degeneration and drain tank (6 free parameters)

gen_v1's four plus L1 (CG degeneration, RLEQ-style Q=12-derived Rs) and LD2 (CS+cascode drain tank).

RLD2 could not be left Q=12-derived from LD2: across a 6000-point search enforcing that constraint, the best achievable worst-case S22 was −7.3 dB (and that point's S11 was around −2 dB). The inherited RLD2=50 Ω with LD2=4 nH is itself only Q≈2.4 — a deliberate heavy-damping choice for this tank, not a coil-loss model, so forcing Q=12 fights the design rather than modeling it. Freeing RLD2 as an independent parameter (keeping RLEQ/RLSHOUT/Rs at Q=12 as usual) immediately found better points than gen_v1's best. ~10,000 evaluations converged on LEQ=1.60 nH, LSHUNT_OUT=4.50 nH, C15=1.84 pF, C11=1.63 pF, L1=5.01 nH (Rs=6.30 Ω), LD2=6.53 nH, RLD2=23.25 Ω (free).

Takeaways

Gain bandwidth and matched bandwidth tell opposite stories here. gen_v2's 62.9% figure is gain-only — S21 stays above 10 dB across a huge span, but S11/S22 only hold ≤−10 dB together across a much narrower 12.9% (306 MHz) window. gen_v1's match actually holds simultaneously good across the widest band of the three, 23.0% (522 MHz) — wider than both gen_v2 (12.9%) and the PEX baseline (17.7%) — despite having less than half gen_v2's gain-only figure.
  • gen_v1 has the widest genuinely-matched band (23.0%, 2.01–2.53 GHz) of all three, plus the highest stability margin (Kmin=248) and a simpler 4-parameter retune. The right default choice if "matched bandwidth" is the spec that matters.
  • gen_v2 wins on peak gain (23.4dB vs 17.4/18.6dB) and NF (2.49dB), and still clears −10dB on both S11 and S22 at 2.4 GHz — but that match narrows faster moving away from center than gen_v1's does, and its gain-bandwidth number isn't a matched-bandwidth number. Right choice if raw gain/NF matter more than how far the match extends, and the lower (but still safe) Kmin=87 is acceptable.
  • The shunt inductors (LEQ, LSHUNT_OUT) are structural, not PEX-specific: every variant keeps them, just retuned in value. Removing them (either direction) hurts badly.
  • RLD2 is a damping/bandwidth-shaping choice, not a coil-loss artifact — the Q=12 convention that works for LEQ/LSHUNT_OUT/Rs does not apply to it.
